utterances.text: You remember the date when your husband came and left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How come you didn't remember the date when what happened to you happened in room B1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean from the 24th -- in the period from the 24th to the 3rd of August, the 24th of July to the 3rd of August, that's when it happened. I didn't remember the date, but it was during that period.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you will agree that it was a terrible event in your life.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my life, yes, it was. It had great impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have no further questions, but I feel the need to make a statement. The witness mentioned that -- she claimed that I phoned her at some given time, about two years ago, and I should like to make the following statement in that regard: Lawyer Zoran Jovanovic was my investigator at the time, and at that time, we learnt that the accused Radic had done what the witness called something good with her husband, parcels and so on, and we considered it necessary to ring her up and ask her whether she wanted to testify on behalf of the accused Radic. I should like to mention that the witness, Witness AT, was not on the list of witnesses attached, and we didn't know that she would appear as a witness, and nobody knew prior to a week ago. When the witness said that she did not wish to testify on behalf of the accused Radic, we left our telephone number, and nobody rang her up after that ever.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I say -- may I ask the gentleman a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may if it's up to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether the gentleman can answer, but ask him. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have just a very short question. Sir, who gave you my telephone number, my private telephone number?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They are investigations which we went into, and I can never tell you, divulge to you how we come by our information. It is my right to phone anybody and to ask them whether they wish to testify on behalf of my client.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. When you phoned me, you introduced yourself saying that you were Fila Filota [sic], the Defence counsel of Mr. Radic. And you first -- the first time you phoned, my husband answered the phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person who called introduced himself in the way I have described. My husband was working and said that I would come home at 6.00 in the evening. When I arrived at 6.00, the telephone rang straight away. I lifted the receiver, and the gentleman on the line introduced himself in that way. I told him that he should not disturb me because it was my private telephone. He said, "Thank you," and said he would not. Before that -- just one moment please. Just one moment. Let me tell my story. Before that, Mr. Krkan's son called me from Prijedor. Now, how come he got my telephone, to be allowed to ring me up on my private phone and disturb me in that way?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness AT, counsel gave you the answer, and you must understand that the Defence counsel has its work to do in defence of their client. Everybody has the right to defend themselves. But finally you have arrived here, and you said -- you told us what Mr. Fila wanted to ask you, and you were allowed to ask Mr. Fila the question. Mr. Fila, have you concluded?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Would Madam Hollis like to ask any questions with respect to this contact with the witness? I'm afraid you didn't understand me. There was a question with respect to the incident concerning communication, telephoning to the witness. It is not for supplementary questions that I'm giving you the floor, just to know whether you have any comments to make with respect to that telephone communication with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Simply, Your Honour, that the witness had informed us of the telephone conversation from the son of Mladjo Radic and her concern about it and asked us if we had given the number, and we explained to her we had not. That would be the only comment that the Prosecution would want to make about any of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The incident is closed. I think that matters have been sufficiently explained. It was a contact on the part of the Defence, that they didn't know at the time that the witness would be called as a Prosecution witness. They were contacting people for themselves. So as a commentary, I don't know if this is legitimate or not, but the witness has arrived here and she came to say what she would have said even if the Defence had called her. So matters have turned out for the best, and that is why we always like to have witnesses here and the examination and cross-examination, which allows both parties to arrive at the truth. Thank you, Mr. Fila, and thank you, Witness AT. I'm now going to give the floor to Mr. Jovan Simic. Mr. Jovan Simic, you have been here with us, and you are aware of the measures that need to be taken in respect of protective measures. Please try to speak slowly and pause between question and answer so that we can follow the debate. I should like to ask Mr. Masic to slow you down if necessary. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. J. Simic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. Good afternoon, Witness AT. My name is Jovan Simic. I'm a lawyer from Belgrade, and together with my colleague Dusan Masic, who is also from Belgrade, I represent the Defence of Mr. Dragoljub Prcac in this case. You testified yesterday that during your stay in Omarska you had seen Mr. Prcac once in the corridor and then a couple of times in the dining area, in the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified yesterday also that you had seen him at the time he was reading out the names of women from a list. Those women were subsequently transferred to Trnopolje, and it took place on the 3rd of August.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you saw him once again, and that on that occasion you asked him what would happen to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have been in constant contact with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you have said, most of the time it was a telephone contact before you came here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In one of such telephone conversations, were you ever asked by the Prosecution if you remembered certain events that you were supposed to testify about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was another subject of one of our conversations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for about one month prior to your testimony here, you did not discuss the events that were the subject of your testimony with the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are the issues which cannot be discussed on the phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a response given to a question by Mr. Fila, you said that you had not seen them for the past month.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean any of the representatives of the OTP.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to ask you the following. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] And I will need the assistance of the usher, please, to give this document to the witness so that she can see what the question is all about. Could you please give it to the witness. For the Prosecution, it is a proffer of the investigator of the 14th of September this year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this is a proffer, so you did not sign it, and you needn't know about its existence. However, I should like to know if you didn't speak to the Prosecutor about the subject of your testimony, and if you didn't see them in the meantime, then either -- we have been provided a document of a different date, but let me put the question to you. I should like to know whether you stated on that occasion or on some other occasion concerning Mr. Prcac, did you say that when you asked him what your fate would be, that he simply shrugged his shoulders and went his way; or did you say what you have stated today in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? When I saw him in the corridor?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should like to know what is correct, what you have said today or what you said on a previous occasion. When you asked him what would happen to you, you said that he had simply shrugged his shoulders on a previous occasion.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And what do you mean what I said today?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Today you said that he had told you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please be asked not to overlap. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he simply shrugged his shoulders and he said that he didn't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day when you saw him, could you tell me precisely on what day it was and at what time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when it happened. It happened after the women had left, (redacted) (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know the exact date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Jovan Simic. Madam Hollis, do you have any additional questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Just two, Your Honour. Re-examined by Ms. Hollis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness AT, during cross-examination by Defence counsel for the accused Radic, you testified that Defence counsel had reminded you of the name of Zeljko Meakic, and that you had spoken about him earlier. To your knowledge, what was Zeljko Meakic's position in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I could tell, his position was above everybody else. He was together with Mr. Prcac. He would be driven in a Mercedes, and he had a personal driver. Everybody addressed him, everybody would go to him, and that is why I concluded that he was superior to all of them, that he was the one who decided on the fate of all of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in your earlier testimony on direct examination when you referred to the superior commander, and you couldn't recall his name, were you referring to Zeljko Meakic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In regard to the incident with Krkan that occurred in room B1, after that incident in B1, did Krkan ever give you food or other gifts after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the food.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Hollis. Judge Fouad Riad has the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Witness AT --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Judge Riad. Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this, I believe, is the moment where I have to indicate why I am on my feet. The witness stated that she had given a statement to the team of the OTP a few years ago, and that on the 14th of September she only spoke to them over the phone. The Defence should now like to hear the Prosecutor on this issue. We should actually like to be given such statements, such proffers, so that we can have that as a basis of our cross-examination. We haven't received any statement of the witness by the Prosecutor. So there are two things that are possible. Either there is a statement and it hasn't been disclosed, or, there are no statements at all. We should like the Prosecutor to make a representation on this particular issue before the witness is released.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila, I believe that the witness said that she had not given a written statement, but that they had had some telephone conversations.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have a look at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila, what statements do you have in mind? What statement are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know. If there is a statement, I should like to see it. That is why I said that we're faced with two possibilities here, either there is no statement, nothing, or there is a statement which has not been disclosed to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila, I will give the floor to Madam Hollis to respond to your objection; however, there is one thing that you should bear in mind. You are venturing into somewhat a dangerous area here. When it comes -- when your turn comes, you will also be asked where are your written statements so that the Prosecutor can also have something on the basis of which they can cross-examine your witnesses. You will be faced with the same questions regarding the truthfulness of the statement, the absence of any pressure or duress, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the statements of my witnesses are already with you in the file that has been provided to you a long time ago, so you needn't worry about that problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Hollis, can you provide us with any clarification regarding this particular issue? Are there any previous statements? Is there a statement which you failed to disclose to the Defence? There is a certain doubt here which needs to be clarified. Let us hear you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, of course the Prosecution is aware that under Rule 66 we must provide prior statements, as well as any statements that would fall under Rule 68. The Prosecution has engaged in contacts with this witness and has the results of those contacts, but not in a written statement form. This witness has never signed a statement based on an interview with the Office of the Prosecutor, so there is no signed statement. That is why the Defence don't have one. As regards the proffer, the 14th of September is the date the proffer was produced. We have never told the Defence that this was a date that we interviewed the witness. It is the date that the proffer was produced. So we gave them a proffer because we have no signed statements from this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: We have given them other statements that appeared to have been signed by the witness, but they were not statements taken by the personnel in the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do apologise, but as regards the 14th of September, I understand that didn't need any answer. On my question, the witness stated, "Yes, I gave a statement." And when I asked her if she had signed the statement, she said, "Of course. Any statement should be signed." That is in the transcript and you can check the record for that. But I have heard the answer of Madam Hollis, and I believe that the issue is closed now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Madam Hollis.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to clarify the record. If you will look at the transcript and if you will follow the next response of the witness, you will see the witness said she didn't remember if she had ever signed a statement or not. So I would suggest that for fairness to the witness, the parties, and the Court, if we are going to refer to the transcript, that we refer to all portions of the transcript that have relevance to the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to solve the issue, but I think that both of you have forgotten to ask the witness. You kept mentioning the Office of the Prosecutor, but maybe the witness spoke to the Unit for Protection of Victims and Witnesses on a number of occasions over the telephone. The witness needn't know who works where, who is a member of the OTP and who is a member of the Unit for Protection of Victims and Witnesses. We all need questions that clarify the issue. The witness said that she had spoken supposedly, because I have certain doubts, with the Office of the Prosecutor several times, and it is also possible that she has spoken with the members of the Unit for Protection of Victims and Witnesses. This should be perhaps clarified. But I don't think we need to go into further details. The witness has had certain telephone contacts and that's that. But I think that we can leave the issue there. I don't think that there is any incident here that needs to be solved. I would now give the floor to Judge Riad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Witness AT, good morning. I'll have to call you AT, although you have a great name, of course. You have been, as I gathered, the president of the women's association in Omarska. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: No. So you're not the president of the women's association in Omarksa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I just would like to have some clarifications concerning Mr. Prcac and Mr. Krkan in the camp. You said that Mr. Prcac used to come usually in the mornings until 2.00, and you heard from the women there that he was a commander. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good. Now, according to your personal observation, did he act as a commander? You mentioned, for instance, that Meakic used to come in a personal driven car and it was very apparent that he was the head. Could you say the same thing on Prcac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't. And I didn't see how Prcac arrived, whether he would come by bus or in a car. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But in the camp itself, was he acting as a commander to be obeyed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him -- I didn't see much of him in Omarksa. I don't know whether he was upstairs in one of the offices on the upper floor. From time to time, he would pass through the kitchen where we women would sit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You said that he would usually be there until 2.00 in the morning, is that right, in general?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, approximately. I don't know whether he stayed longer and I didn't see him. I would see him when he came to the camp, and I think that he left around 1.00 or 2.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: When you mentioned that you would -- that you saw corpses and bodies being thrown out of the "white house" and trucks were loaded with corpses, was that happening also during the day, in the morning, or at night in darkness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the day, I was able to see the bodies being thrown out of the "white house," and in the evening, around half past seven or 8.00, the bodies were driven away in a small TAM truck which passed by our window, and we could see it passing by through the curtains that were on those windows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: So the bodies were thrown out of the "white house" during the day and everybody can see it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not everybody could see it. We, the women, were behind the curtain. As I was distributing the food and washing the dishes, I could glance from time to time through the window and see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Could they be seen from the commanders' office? I think it was -- was it B1? What was it exactly, the room of the commanders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The commanders' room was across the corridor from B5. B5 was the commanders' room, and B11 and B12 had the windows facing towards the "white house."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You also mentioned that on the 3rd of August, Mr. Prcac was calling the detainees to be transferred. Was that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And he kept two people. He kept two men.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was the one who kept people. The people who were called out were put aside, men and women, and then they were separated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: When they are called out, you mean he was doing the calling out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And you do not know why they were kept and -- why these two men were kept and what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You were also kept, I think (redacted) you were kept with (redacted).

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Where were you kept? Do you know? Were you needed --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. To this date I haven't been able to find out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: What services did you render in this part when you were kept? What kind of services were you asked for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same as up until then. I was distributing food and doing the cleaning work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you just a question about Mr. Krkan. You mentioned that -- perhaps we can go into a private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Have you an idea where these people were taken?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not yet Judge Riad, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You said that 170 men were taken away on the 3rd of August. They were called by, I think, Mr. Prcac, as you saw. Do you know where they were taken? Were they liberated? Were they taken to another camp? What happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those people were not called out by Mr. Prcac. They remained behind with 5 women and 172 men, and they were subsequently registered by the High Commissioner and taken to Manjaca. As far as I know, they're all alive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, too, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Judge Riad. Madam Judge Wald has the floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Thank you. I just have three questions, Witness AT. You said early on in your testimony that sometimes when you were working in the kitchen and you tried to give the detainees a little extra food, that the guards would, I think, poke you or, you know, tell you that you couldn't do that. My question is this: Who told you to begin with how much food you could give the detainees? If you were passing out the food, who instructed you as to how much food you could give any one of the detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: While all the women were there, I worked every other day. (redacted) (redacted). Three men in military uniform would stand behind my back, and they told me to put a ladle of soup in every plate. I don't know if it was just a thin soup or whether some pieces of other food were inside as well. So that was the portion that I could give out, together with a small piece of bread.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Were these men in military uniforms part of the regular security guards, or were they special people that only stayed for the kitchen, for the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was only one man who was in charge of the kitchen, and the other two were most probably from -- belonged to the guards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. So that the one person who was in charge of the kitchen, was that the only thing he did? Could you tell who he reported to or not, who gave him his orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. My other question is, when Mr. Krkan told you

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: (redacted)? Did he give you any idea of why you would be in one group and others might be in another group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't give any explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, too, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness AT, I, too, have a few questions for you. Concerning the bodies and the truck which transported them, you said first of all that it was 7.00; however, in a response to a question by my colleague, you said that it was sometime between 7.00 and 8.00. That is not the problem; however, I should like to know how and why you knew that it was 7.00 or 8.00 at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: At 7.00 a.m. we would go to the kitchen and we would spend 12 hours in the kitchen. So when they realised that it was 7.00, we would be taken back to the rooms where we slept.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have another question for you. As you have probably realised, there is something that needs to be clarified here with you. You made some contacts with the Tribunal over the telephone. Those contacts, were they always contacts with the members of the Prosecution, or did you contact some other employees of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received a telephone number of a young woman who spoke my language, and mostly we would discuss my papers and my stay here, and my trip here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you say papers and your stay and your trip here, it had something to do with your testimony here at the Tribunal. What kind of papers do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The papers that would allow me to stay here. If I have only a brief, temporary visa, then it is very difficult for me to travel. The police in my place of residence is supposed to issued me a long-term visa. So every time I would tell this young woman that it was impossible for me to travel here on a short-term visa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In response to a question that was put to you by Defence counsel, you reacted spontaneously, and you said, "By telephone we cannot discuss such matters." What kind of matters did you have in mind exactly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had in mind long conversations that cannot take place over the telephone. In my opinion, one should only discuss brief matters over the telephone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. That means that you used the telephone only for the purpose of your trip and the necessary arrangements that had to be done in that respect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me go to another area, Witness AT. You said that Krkan had given you food and water that he himself ate and drank, and you said that you were able at that point to tell the difference. What was the difference?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The food that I received was the same food eaten by the police and the guards. It was actually their leftovers. We got some hamburgers and some soup full of vegetables in it and pieces of meat. And that is how I came to the conclusion that their food was more nutritious and of better quality than the food that was eaten by the detainees. I had an opportunity to drink water from a plastic jerrycan because that was the water that they drank, and I wanted to be taken to that spring, to that source. And indeed, (redacted) were allowed to go there to the spring, and we had a chance to drink that water. So that is how I came to the conclusion that there was a difference both in terms of food and water.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know where the food was prepared?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The food was prepared at the Separacija, both for them and for us. I was once hidden away there in the building of Separacija, and we were given a meal there when we were taken to clean the area there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness, for your answers. You have come to the end of your testimony here at the Tribunal. I must say that you are now a free woman, and you do have an opportunity to enjoy life. There are always things that can be celebrated, for example, a birthday or things like that. Thank you very much for coming here to testify, and we are fully aware of the hard times you have been through. At the end of this testimony, I should like to ask you whether there is anything that you wish to say, anything that hasn't been asked of you so far.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if you will allow me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness AT, let us hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I should like to thank you all for enabling me to testify here, and I should also like to thank you for your kindness and your understanding. However, I have a question for you which I would like to ask with your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have a question for me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As a business woman, a former business woman, I had a very good situation. I should like to know who is going to compensate me for the damage that has been done to me, including my health condition and all the loss of property that I sustained. I should like to ask you and also ask a question to the gentleman who did this to me, I should like to know how this future can be restored for me, because I have lost so much, and I don't want to lose hope. I have to live with something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness AT, we have heard your question. It's a question for all of us to reflect upon. I do not have a concrete answer to give you. The only thing I can tell you is that we, too, are concerned with the issue you have just brought up. You must be assured that there are people who think about this problem and who are tying to find a more specific and more concrete answer to the question that you have asked of all of us. I have to refer to you as Witness AT because I do not wish to disclose your identity in any way, but once again, thank you very much for coming here to testify, and let me now ask the usher to help the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, do not move. We will resume at half past three. We're ten minutes delayed. I think that instead of starting at half past three we should perhaps start at 35 minutes past three so that we have at least some time. So instead of half past three, we will start at 35 minutes past 3.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 2.38 p.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. We have our next witness, Witness U. Mr. Saxon, I see that you're in the right place to give me the answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. The next witness for the Prosecution will be Witness U.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President, but I have to request that as evidence, what I used be accepted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite right, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Judge. Microphone, please, for the President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Yes. It is D30/A and B; is that right? Yes, D30/A. Any exhibits to tender, Ms. Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Anything to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, and we have no objection to the Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Exhibits D30/A and B have been admitted. Thank you very much, Mr. Fila, for bringing that to our attention. It was on my mind but it just slipped my mind. We can call the witness now, Witness U. Would the usher have the witness shown in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. President, while we're waiting, have Your Honours received the summary points that I prepared for this witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Saxon, we have received points for direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps while we're waiting, could I ask the representative of the Registrar whether the voice distortion is working.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, it's working.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's fine now. That was between me and the interpreters. Witness U, can you hear me properly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're going to read the solemn declaration handed to you by the usher, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The usher is now going to show you a piece of paper with your name on it. After having looked at the piece of paper, please tell us by giving us a yes or no answer whether it is indeed your name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I'd like to say thank you for coming here, Witness U. We're going to refer to you as Witness U for the reasons that are well known to you. You're now going to be answering questions put to you by the Prosecutor, and, afterwards, you will be answering questions put to you by the Defence counsel and the Judges. Your witness, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you Your Honour. Examined by Mr. Saxon:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, are you from the Prijedor region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: I'm a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could briefly go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm about to ask the witness a few questions which would provide persons watching with her identity, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Mr. Saxon, but we said that whenever a private session is requested, that the reasons for that should be stated in advance. We're now going to move into private session for several moments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in public session, Mr. Saxon. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, was your husband detained by Serb forces in mid-June 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Initially, where was your husband confined?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: In Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Eventually, did you try to go to Keraterm to try to see your husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how many times did you go to Keraterm for this purpose?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately when was the first time that you went to the Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: In mid-June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you bring anything with you for your husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Food and clothing, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you neared the entrance to the Keraterm camp, were you alone, or were there others there with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: There were other people around me, but I don't know how many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened as you got closer to the entrance to the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: The guards who were at the gate fired from some firearms, fired by my feet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say they fired by your feet, does that mean where you saw the bullets land?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say they fired by your feet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Well, they probably wanted to frighten me, not to go near the gate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the shooting, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: A guard came up to me whom I knew, but I didn't know his name. He took the bag and said that he would give the bag to my husband, and I returned home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, did you see your husband on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes, but he was far off. He was quite far off from the gate. I could see him amongst many other people who were in Keraterm at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did your husband look at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: He was very thin and exhausted; he had a beard; he was unkept. Like all the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, approximately when was the second time that you went to Keraterm to try to see your husband?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: It was at the end of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did you bring on this second occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: I think that it was food on that occasion. I can't remember that I had taken any clothing with me, but there was food, certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it morning or afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, as you approached the entrance to the Keraterm camp, who did you see there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: While I was approaching the entrance, there were the guards quite normally, but I don't know who they were. When I arrived at the entrance, I was able to see all the people in the Keraterm camp, and I saw my husband there, too, who was standing in front of the group. And at that time while I was approaching, Mr. Zigic recognised me, and he took my husband under his arm and took him towards the entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, when you refer to Mr. Zigic, do you know Mr. Zigic's first name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Zoran.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Zoran Zigic before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know Zoran Zigic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: I knew him from before. We went to the same school. It was the same eight-year school, elementary school, and we lived in the same area more or less. So I knew him well. Afterwards, he worked as a taxi driver, but, generally speaking, I knew him very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How was Zoran Zigic dressed that day when you saw him at the Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Zoran was wearing a military uniform at the time, a cap that is called a beret. It was red.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did Zoran Zigic do at that time when you approached the entrance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: When they came up together, not that near, not right up to the fence, I was standing there, and I quote his words now, he said, "Here. Take a good look at your husband. He's going to fall first for the freedom of this town."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just so that the record is clear, when you say that "they came up together," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Zigic and my husband.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did your husband come closer to you under his own free will or did someone lead him there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Zigic was leading him without any force. He had locked arms with him. They were approaching arm in arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did your husband look when you saw him at that moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: He was very thin, looked exhausted. He had an even bigger beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did your husband say anything to you at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: No. After Zigic's words, he just looked at me and I saw two tears falling down his face, and that was our last meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since that day, have you ever seen your husband again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, I'd like you to turn your --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, I'd like you to turn your mind to your own detention eight years ago. Were you detained by Serb forces on the 14th of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were the men who detained you dressed that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: They were wearing police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you describe the colour or colours of those uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Light blue shirts with short sleeves and trousers of a grey-blue colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time on the 14th of June [sic], were you detained alone or with other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: With other people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I misspoke. I should have said in my question "at that time on the 14th of July." Do you recall the names of some of the other persons you were detained with at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes. (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was her name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Zlata Bilajac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnicity of Zlata Bilajac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: She was Muslim. Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you and Zlata Bilajac detained with anyone else.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes. There were some men from my building, but I cannot now recollect their exact names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Initially, Witness U, where were you, Zlata Bilajac, and the men taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: To Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you taken there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: In a police car that we used to call Marica or Black Marija. And while going there, we couldn't see where we were going, but only once we arrived at Keraterm did I realise where we were, that we were in Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When that car stopped at Keraterm, what part of the camp did it stop at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Roughly about 5 metres, 5 or 10 metres, as far as I can remember, away from the people who were already detained there. To the right there was room where they ordered us to take off our jewellery and all other valuables. It was a room in which there were guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "we were ordered to take off all of our valuables, jewellery and valuables," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: A man called Sikirica who was on duty in the Keraterm camp that day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know this man from before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: From the town. I would come across him. He was employed in a factory called Cellulose, but I would also come across him on my way back from work or simply walking in town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you arrived in Keraterm, what, if anything, did this man named Sikirica say to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: He ordered that we take off our jewellery and everything we had on us, but he didn't address me personally. And when they started hitting the men who had arrived with us, he then said, "I am the commander here," and I'm quoting his words. And he also took part in the beatings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, where were you and Zlata Bilajac taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: We were put together with a group of men. It was very hot, and as far as I can remember, this whole area was open so that in this group of men, I found quite a number of friends. There was a cousin of mine among them. I could see his tears. And they moved away to make room for us to sit down. There were very many men there. So we sat down on some wooden pallets that were on the ground, if you know what pallets are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, let's go a little bit slower. As the day went by and night began to fall, what, if anything, happened to you and Zlata Bilajac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: A man came up. His name was Nedeljko Timarac, a man I knew from before. He was wearing a military uniform. His hat was a military one, and he asked the two of us to go with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you know Nedeljko Timarac from before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Nedeljko Timarac also went with me to the same (redacted) (redacted) so that I know him very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that Nedeljko -- now, you said that Nedeljko Timarac was wearing a military uniform that day and a military hat. What colour was his military hat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Grey.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you refer to a military hat, are you referring to a beret which you described as Zoran Zigic wearing previously, or something different?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: No. This is a different type of hat. What Mr. Zigic was wearing is called a beret, whereas Nedeljko had a hat with a visor, a different kind of hat, which we call a cap.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe what Nedeljko looked like at that time in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: He was slim, thin, I must say he was distinctly ugly with a long nose, without teeth. That's all I can say as a description.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did Nedeljko Timarac take you and Zlata Bilajac that afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: The two of us went with him. He took us inside the Keraterm building where the offices used to be before the war. I cannot remember now whether this was the second or third building. As far as I remember, it was the first floor. When we entered the corridor, to the left he put Zlata in one room, and he went on with me the length of the corridor to the end of it, and he entered this other room together with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after you entered this other room with Nedeljko Timarac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: In that office there was a table. I could feel it with my fingers, because it was dark. He told me to climb on the table, and he raped me on that table.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Nedeljko Timarac raped you on that table, what happened later that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: He left without saying a word. I remained on the table. After that, other men came in. I don't know exactly how many -- there were many -- who also raped me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, when you say that these men raped you, do you mean that they penetrated you with their penis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you spend the remainder of the night in that office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: I think that I lost consciousness, and in the morning I woke up, and when I looked around, I could see that I was lying in a pool of blood. Just then a guard came in, someone I didn't know. I could notice shock on his face, too. He ordered me to wash. I got up, reached a tap with water and tried to wash myself. He waited for me and took me outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When this guard took you outside, where did he take you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: I was going back to the yard. He told me to sit down on a rock, and there I could see the detainees once more, the people who were in Keraterm. I was able to see well. I was very confused, and they were all staring at me, probably the way I looked. In any event, they witnessed my appearance that morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much time did you spend sitting on that stone or rock?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it might have been a couple of hours, two or three, as far as I can recollect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, what condition were your clothes in, were your clothes like at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: My clothes were bloodstained. There were stains on my blouse and trousers. More on the trousers. I managed to wash some of it off but many stains remained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the colour of your blouse and trousers that you were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: My trousers were from rayon, greyish-green, and my shirt was silk, mauve-ish green. Before that I was wearing a sweater in mauve, and that sweater or cardigan was left behind in the room where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you wear that same shirt during the remainder of your detention by Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you sat on that stone, did any of the Keraterm guards or camp personnel speak to you during that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When, if ever, did you see Zlata Bilajac that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes, did I see her. Immediately after bringing me, the same guard brought Zlata Bilajac, who sat -- again, I think it was a stone. It could have been something else. She was about 3 or 4 metres away from me. We didn't have any contact. We just stared at each other without uttering a word.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, when you saw Zlata Bilajac that morning, what did you observe about her appearance at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Terribly frightened, red in the face, tears in her eyes. She was crying.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any Keraterm camp personnel offer you assistance that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After noon on that day, where did you and Zlata Bilajac go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: To Omarska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you travel to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: A police van came for us. The same one that we called Marica or Black Marija. From other side they brought a group of men. I don't know exactly how many. Six or seven most probably, not fewer than that, and the two of us, and they boarded us onto the van and then we set off. Again, we didn't know where they were taking us. When we arrived at Omarska the van stopped, and when we got off, we realised where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, what happened to the men in your van when the van stopped at the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: As soon as we got off the van, the guards who were in the compound close to the van that same moment started beating the men using various objects.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you and Zlata Bilajac taken at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: At that moment, a guard took us to the "white house."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you entered the "white house," what, if anything, could you see in the different rooms there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes. As we were passing through the corridor, to the right and the left were rooms. First I heard cries, moans. I just know that that house looked awful. It was covered in blood. And the men I managed to see were lying down to the left on the floor in blood, and to my right I managed to see two other men, I think, who were also lying in -- lying beaten up and covered in blood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What part of the "white house" did you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What part of the "white house" did you and Zlata Bilajac go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: It was a part that you found as you entered the "white house." At the end of the corridor there was a room. At the end, at the end of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if at this time I could ask the usher to assist me. I have a photograph that I've marked as Prosecution Exhibit 3/148, and if a copy could be placed on an ELMO by the witness and copies distributed to the Judges and to Defence counsel, please. Thank you. Could the ELMO be moved a little bit closer perhaps to the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the microphone be moved closer to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, does this photograph show the interior of the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that photograph, what is the number of the room inside the "white house" where you and Zlata Bilajac went to that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: The number marked as A5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you pick up the pen or one of the pens that's in front of you, please, and mark inside that room the letter "U" and the letters "ZB" to indicate where you and Zlata were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How long were you and Zlata Bilajac inside that room marked A5 on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Approximately two to three hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kinds of sounds, if any, could you hear as you sat in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes, I could hear sounds. All the time while we were there, one could hear screams, crying, guards who were beating men. They were yelling, cursing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What conversations, if any, did you overhear while you sat in the room marked A5?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes. When the guards beat the men, they would curse, and I quote, "Fuck your balija mothers, your Ustasha mothers. You all need to be killed."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you overhear any other discussions between guards in the corridor of the "white house" at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you sat in that room in the "white house," did anyone else enter the "white house" and try to get near you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes. A group of guards set off towards the two of us, but one guard stopped them, and I quote, he said, "Don't approach those women," and they turned back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, eventually that day, were you taken out of the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who removed you from the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: A guard came whom I didn't know, and he took us out from the "white house."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you left the "white house" that day, what, if anything, did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes. When I was leaving the "white house," to the right of the "white house" I saw a couple of bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say to the right, were the bodies in front of you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mike, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say the phrase "to the right of the `white house,'" were the bodies in front of the "white house," or to the side of the "white house," or both?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Should I repeat my question, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what happened. We didn't get an answer from the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, when you say the phrase "to the right of the `white house,'" were the bodies in front of the "white house," to the side of the "white house," or both?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Mr. Krstan Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we're having difficulties with the translation. It's not coming through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. As we have voice distortion, I think you have to switch to channel 8, I think. Is that okay now? Yes? Witness U, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it's all right. We can continue, Mr. Saxon. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, when you say you saw bodies to the right of the "white house," were the bodies in front of the "white house," to the side of the "white house," or both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: In front and to the side, to the right. In front and next to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you could please assist me again. If you could remove the photograph that's next to the witness, and place this photograph which I have marked as Prosecution Exhibit 3/149. If a copy could be provided to the registry, the Judges, and to Defence counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, I'd like to ask you to draw your attention to the photograph on the machine next to you. Does that photograph show the area in front and to the sides of the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please pick up the pen again and draw "X's" on this photograph where you saw bodies on that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, during the remainder of your detention in Omarska, how often would you see bodies near the "white house"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Later on, not so often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about earlier on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Well, you could see -- if I was able to see from the restaurant, you could see a body or two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krstan Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my objection refers to the formulation of that question. The witness said that she saw this for the first time, and then the Prosecutor asked her how much before that she had seen them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not quite sure about that. I think that I heard the witness say that she didn't see them afterwards and that the Prosecutor asked about before. But let's have Mr. Saxon to respond to the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, we may have a problem with translation or terminology. I asked the witness, "During the remainder of your detention in Omarksa, how much would you see bodies near the "white house"?" The witness responded, "Later on, not so often." So then I asked another question. I said, "Well, what about earlier on? In other words, sooner in time?" I asked a different question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That was more or less what I heard. But anyway, Mr. Krstan Simic, I have to reject your objection, overrule it. The question was legitimate. Please go ahead, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think the witness has answered the question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, from the "white house" that day, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: The restaurant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did the women confined in the restaurant building sleep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: On the first floor. In the offices which, before the war, were offices belonging to the mine. So in the offices. The rooms where the offices had been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the women sleep in all of these offices or a limited number of the offices?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Two offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if I could ask for your assistance again. If you could place one of these diagrams which has been marked as 3/150 on the ELMO and provide copies to the registrar, the Chamber, and the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, does this diagram --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- show rooms on the first floor the restaurant building? I'll rephrase my question again. Witness U, does this diagram show the rooms on the first floor of this restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the number of the sleeping room where you slept?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you pick up the pen that's in front of you and write the letter "U" inside that room, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Usher, if you could, would you remove that photograph, please, that diagram. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, where would the women confined in the building, like yourself, spend their days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: In the restaurant area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to the armed conflict in 1992, were you familiar with a man named Dragoljub Prcac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you familiar with this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: I met him frequently. (redacted) (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where he worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: No. I didn't know before, but I learnt it subsequently in the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When, if ever, did you learn the name of this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: When I arrived at the camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you learn the name of this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: From the women who were detained there. They said that his name was Mr. Prcac and that he was the camp commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, how often would you see Dragoljub Prcac in Omarksa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Not often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that the women in the camp told you that Mr. Prcac was the camp commander. What did you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: I said "upravnik" "warden."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me finish my question, please. What did you observe that led you to believe that Dragoljub Prcac was a commander or a warden?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, Witness U. Mr. Jovan Simic? MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness said that he was the upravnik, that is to say, the warden, not the camp commander. And we think that it would be a good idea if the Prosecution were not to interrupt all the time so that we can hear what she says. My objection has to do with the fact that she said "warden" and not "commander," as it says in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Jovan Simic. As you can see, in the transcript we haven't got the word, but you probably heard the word used because you understand the language. Mr. Krstan Simic, what is your objection? One by one, please. Mr. Krstan Simic now. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my objection is the following: The method of examination. The witness said that she heard that Mr. Prcac was the warden, and then the question was, "How did you come to believe that he was the warden?" And there was no mention of her belief in what he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: There is no mention because the witness has already answered. [Interpretation] I think that we -- we don't understand the language spoken by the witness, so we weren't able to understand the point of your objection. The witness -- that is to say, that part was not translated. Now, the objection made by Mr. Krstan Simic was one -- I don't think that you're right, because if the witness said "warden" or "commander," that is legitimate. It is a conclusion made by the witness. Now you can ask her how she arrived at that conclusion. I don't know why you're objecting, Mr. Krstan Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me be more specific. The witness said that she had heard from other women that Mr. Prcac was the warden, and then the next question was a simple one "On the basis -- what did you base your belief that he was the commander? What did you base that assumption on?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, would you like to add anything? I see that you were going to say something. MR. J. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I was going to say the same thing, Your Honour, make the same objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very well. Mr. Saxon, I would like to hear you. I think you have understood the meaning of the objection made. I did not understand it, to be frank, to begin with, but go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Nor did I, Your Honour. I think I can ask my question in a different way that hopefully would be better received by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Now, if the witness says to you that she heard from other women, from the other women that Mr. Prcac was the warden or commander, then you can't ask her straight away what led you to make that conclusion. You should ask the witness, "Did you ask the other women what they observed and what led them to conclude that?" It's a bit complicated, but you have understood the point, so please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to ask the witness what she observed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, what, if anything, did you observe regarding the responsibility or position of Drago Prcac in the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: I can only say that at the end of our stay in the camp Mr. Drago Prcac came with a list of women who were to go home, and because of that, I concluded that he could be a warden or something of that kind. That is all I can say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's talk about that last day in the Omarska camp, Witness U. Do you recall the date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: It was the 3rd of August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time of the day on the 3rd of August did you see Dragoljub Prcac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: It was morning, 9.00 or 10.00 as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: In the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you see Dragoljub Prcac do at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: He went into the restaurant. He said, "Women, I'm going to read out a list to you. You're going home." I remember those words of his. And he proceeded to read out a list of women.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you recall, who were the women that were going home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes. Nuska Sivac, Jadranka Cigelj, Hatidza Alagic, Zlata Cikota. I was among them. (redacted)-- no, no, that's a mistake. I think that's enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if I could ask your assistance, please. I have a diagram that's been marked as Prosecution Exhibit 3/151. A copy to be placed next to the witness and distributed, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, if you could turn your attention to that diagram.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, if you could turn your attention to the diagram that's been placed next to you. Does this diagram depict the ground floor of the restaurant building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please mark the area where you were sitting on the morning of the 3rd of August with the letter "U."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please mark the spot where you saw Dragoljub Prcac that morning with the letters "DP."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness U, did a bus come to Omarska that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you and the rest of your group of women get on that bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did that bus take you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: To Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which women stayed behind in the Omarska camp on the 3rd of August?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS U
utterances.text: Mugbila Besirevic; (redacted); Zdenka, I can't remember her surname now. I can't remember the name of one other woman whom I think was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
